ety.text: Uncertain. The name has been compared to English altar or Russian янта́рь (jantárʹ, “amber”). Viktor Martynov derives the name from Iranic *al-atar, literally “white-burning”, the synonym си́ний ка́мень (sínij kámenʹ, “blue stone”) being a calque. Cognate with Ukrainian ала́тир (alátyr).

ety.text: Omitting several steps, from Ancient Greek κεράτιον (kerátion), from κέρας (kéras). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂- (“head, top; horn”). Compare typologically гран (gran) (< Latin grānum, via PIE cognate with зерно́ (zernó)).

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic прочь (pročĭ, “away”), from Proto-Slavic *pročь. Per Vasmer…
